ratings_source: Google Maps star rating (one decimal) read in a logged-out browser on 2026-09-29; the limited view withheld review counts and review text.

excluded_non_mains: Guide entries that sell only desserts, bakes or drinks (for example Mister Donut, fieldnotes, 108 Matcha Saro, Wunderfolks, Gokoku, CHURN, Mango Ice, Ji De Chi, Markozar, Tiong Bahru Bakery, Luckin Coffee, Wanpo, Jamba, rrooll, ROYCE', Cellarbration, Puff and Peaks, The Hainan Story) are outside a ranking of places to eat a main.

places.name: TANYU

quotes.eatbook-tampines-1: grilled fish is soaked in a green pepper-infused broth
quotes.wtdit-tampines-1: The fish is grilled to perfection and served in a bubbling, aromatic broth infused with green peppercorns.

places.summary: Whole Chongqing-style grilled fish from a Shenzhen chain, served in bubbling broths such as fresh green pepper. All three guides single out tender fish and bold, numbing heat; a fish (about $48.90 to $55.50++) is meant for sharing.

dishes.name: Grilled Fish with Fresh Green Pepper
dishes.note: One diner's share of a spicy Sichuan broth pot for 2-3.

places.name: Abundance

quotes.eatbook-tampines: thick-cut noodles are topped with stir-fried minced pork and a century egg sauce

places.summary: Taiwanese comfort food and craft beer. Eatbook calls out the gua bao of braised pork belly, peanuts, pickles and coriander, and thick noodles under minced pork with a century-egg sauce.

places.name: The Tree Cafe

quotes.sethlui-century-square: gorgeous wall murals (all of which are hand-painted by its creative team), a swing chair, soft velvety chairs, and plenty of greenery and fairy lights

places.summary: A brunch cafe that SETHLUI rates as much for its hand-painted murals, swing chair and greenery as for its food: big breakfasts, chicken and waffles, and steak plates at $11.50 to $18.90.

places.name: Hawkers' Street

quotes.wtdit-tampines-1: Their handmade mee hoon kway is soft yet springy, soaking up the rich, flavourful broth with every bite.
quotes.eatbook-tampines-1: springy egg noodles tossed in a chilli sauce and lard mix, topped with char siew

places.summary: A 12-stall food court with Michelin Bib Gourmand names (Tai Wah Pork Noodle, Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice) and Jiak Song's handmade mee hoon kway, which reviewers call soft yet springy. Mains start at about $5.

places.name: Genki Sushi

quotes.wtdit-tampines-mall: Each dish is packed with flavor and freshness, making it hard to stop at just one plate.

places.summary: Sushi sent to your seat on bullet-train carts. Reviewers praise fresh, flavour-packed plates from $2.90 but warn of peak-hour queues.

places.name: Legendary Hong Kong

quotes.wtdit-tampines-mall: Stepping inside feels just like a cha chaan teng in Hong Kong with its signature tiles and nostalgic furniture.

places.summary: A cha chaan teng styled on Hong Kong, with a four-meat roast platter, cart noodles with 22 toppings and eggy HK French toast. Roast meats sell out by dinner, so go early.

dishes.name: Roast duck on rice
dishes.note: One diner's share of the roast platter.

dishes.name: Roast pork on rice
dishes.note: Stands in for the crispy pork belly.

places.name: Butahage

quotes.eatbook-tampines: 90-year-old secret sauce that's smoky, savoury, and sweet

places.summary: Obihiro-style butadon: grilled Spanish pork loin on short-grain rice, glazed with what Eatbook describes as a smoky, savoury and sweet 90-year-old sauce. From $11.80++.

places.name: Keming Bing Sat

quotes.eatbook-tampines-1: featuring seven pieces of thick-cut char siew, two sunny-side-up eggs, and kai lan over Wuchang rice

places.summary: A popular Hong Kong cafe. The signature plate is thick-cut char siew over Wuchang rice with two sunny-side-up eggs ($10.90++), with milk tea poured over a bear-shaped ice cube.

dishes.name: Char Siew Rice with two eggs

places.name: Ging Sun Ho King of Bun

quotes.dfd-tampines-mall: The buns are best eaten hot, with the thin crust giving a clean bite before the soup is released.

places.summary: Sheng jian bao made fresh on site, with crisp golden bottoms and a pork-and-soup filling that bursts when bitten, plus nutty dan dan noodles. Both reviewers say eat them hot.

places.name: Haidilao Hot Pot

quotes.sethlui-century-square: Tomato Soup and Haidilao-styled Bai-Yu Soup are go-to choices

places.summary: Hot pot with custom broths; SETHLUI's picks are the tomato and bai-yu soups with pork belly and beef. Open until 2am, the latest in the hub.

dishes.name: Tomato soup hot pot, one person
dishes.note: Your total depends on what you add to the pot.

places.name: Monster Planet

quotes.eatbook-tampines-1: Crepes are made fresh to order and come in a range of flavours

places.summary: Halal-certified Japanese curry rice paired with crepes made to order. The $15.90++ chicken katsu curry is the main to order.

places.name: Seorae Jib

quotes.wtdit-tampines-mall: Tender, flavorful, and perfectly grilled, it's the highlight of the menu and keeps me coming back.

places.summary: Korean BBQ built around galmaegisal (pork skirt), which the reviewer calls tender and perfectly grilled, with free-flow sides. Asking staff to grill at the table cuts down the smoke.

dishes.name: Galmaegisal (pork skirt) with rice
dishes.note: Grilled pork on rice; free-flow sides not counted.

places.name: Swensen's

quotes.sethlui-tampines-mall: More than 180 flavours of ice cream have been created since Earle Swensen established his first ice cream shop in San Francisco in 1948!

places.summary: A family restaurant best known for ice cream sundaes, which also serves Western mains such as lasagne and baked rice for about $15.

places.name: Bari Bari Steak

quotes.eatbook-tampines-1: Each steak is served medium rare on a hot stone pellet heated to 300°C, allowing diners to finish cooking

places.summary: A Hong Kong teppan chain. Steaks arrive medium-rare on a stone heated to 300°C so you finish them at the table; $22.90 to $25.90++ including a salad bar.

dishes.name: Australian Flank Steak Teppan
dishes.note: Meat only; rice and salad bar not counted.

places.name: Nanyang Dao

quotes.eatbook-tampines: Huge bowl of yellow noodles is topped with beancurd skin, boiled egg, fried pork belly, and prawns, then doused with a rich and hearty curry.

places.summary: Malaysian classics. Eatbook's pick is a big bowl of curry mee with fried pork belly, prawns, egg and beancurd skin in a rich curry ($9.90++), which it says rivals the popular chains.

dishes.name: Seleyang Big Bowl Curry Mee
dishes.note: Eatbook's bowl adds pork belly and prawns.

places.name: Sushi Zanmai

quotes.dfd-tampines-mall: The broth came bright and lively, with a heat that built slowly, wrapping itself around the sweetness of the vegetables and the meat.

places.summary: A sushi chain with a long menu. DanielFoodDiary liked a spicy niku nabe whose heat builds slowly, alongside chirashi dons and nigiri.

places.name: Kuan Zhai Alley

quotes.dfd-tampines-mall: The vermicelli absorbed the sauce and sweetness of the prawns as it cooked, creating a savoury base with gentle seafood flavours.

places.summary: Sichuan comfort food served in claypots. The braised prawns cook down into bean vermicelli that soaks up a savoury, gently sweet sauce ($18.80).

places.name: OPPA Bibimbap

quotes.wtdit-tampines-1: Each bowl arrives with a satisfying crackle, the rice forming a crispy golden crust at the bottom.

places.summary: Hot-stone bibimbap that arrives crackling over a crisp rice crust, in generous portions, with cheese and seasonal unagi versions.

places.name: Namu Bulgogi

quotes.sethlui-tampines-1: perfectly grilled meats that are juicy, tender, and infused with a distinct smoky aroma.

places.summary: A Korean grill using imported oakwood, praised for juicy, smoky meats, with an eight-hour oxtail and tteokbokki on the side.

dishes.name: Beef bulgogi with rice
dishes.note: One person's share of a grill set.

places.name: Tongue Tip Lanzhou Beef Noodles

quotes.sethlui-century-square: clear beef broth is comforting yet full-bodied, while its beef slices are tender and meaty

places.summary: Halal hand-pulled Lanzhou noodles in eight thicknesses. The clear broth is comforting yet full-bodied and the beef tender ($10.90 to $13.90).
